name: Bastien Nkrumah-Ostrowski
subcategory: corporate art director / subversive AR muralist
creator: Bastien Nkrumah-Ostrowski
description: By day, Nkrumah-Ostrowski is Senior Visual Architect at Axiom Media's Tier 3-4 content division, designing the aspirational skyline aesthetics that appear in sponsored neural feeds across GLMZ. By night, under the tag PALE COAT, he deploys unauthorized augmented reality overlays onto corporate public sculpture — transforming commissioned vanity pieces in Crown District and the mid-Spire atrium concourses into deteriorating ruins, revealed only to users running unlicensed AR filters. His double life has been an open secret in underground art circles for nearly a decade.
medium: augmented reality (unauthorized overlay, unlicensed AR filter distribution) and corporate neural-feed design (licensed)
cultural_impact: PALE COAT's overlays have become a pilgrimage circuit for mid-tier creatives disillusioned with corporate aesthetics — the act of installing the illegal filter and walking the Crown District 'ruin route' is itself a countercultural ritual.
controversy: Axiom Media conducted an internal investigation in 2211 that came within one informant of identifying him; the investigation was quietly shelved, fueling speculation that someone in Axiom's upper management is a PALE COAT admirer or co-conspirator. Nkrumah-Ostrowski has never confirmed or denied the identity publicly.
story_hooks: A junior Axiom investigator stumbles onto genuine proof of Nkrumah-Ostrowski's double identity and must decide whether to report it, leverage it, or destroy the evidence — each choice carrying its own lethal implications.

PALE COAT's newest overlay unexpectedly reveals what appears to be accurate architectural data about a sealed sub-level beneath a Spire atrium — data Nkrumah-Ostrowski insists he never planted, suggesting someone is using his tag as a dead-drop.

A Tier 5 collector wants to commission PALE COAT for a private installation — not knowing the artist works for their own media subsidiary — and the negotiation threatens to collapse Nkrumah-Ostrowski's carefully maintained separation.
